title: Lottie animation playback in React
summary: Render and control Lottie animations in a React web application. Compare the JSON-first lottie-web and lottie-react line with the DotLottie player line, including .lottie support, React integration, runtime assets, maintenance, licensing and browser cost.
constraints: Permissive license across the full dependency tree
React 18 and 19 supported when a React wrapper is used
Browser playback; SSR is optional and client-only is acceptable
Actively maintained: a release within 12 months across the chosen runtime stack
No unfixed high or critical advisories
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Runtime assets such as WASM or workers must be self-hostable; no mandatory CDN dependency
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap
out_of_scope: Choosing an animation asset pipeline or CDN
React Native and native mobile players
Detailed art-direction review of individual animations
notes: The user prefers React and accepts client-only rendering. lottie-web is the long-standing JSON renderer but has not shipped since May 2025; lottie-react is an active wrapper around it. The DotLottie line is active, provenance-signed and supports both Lottie JSON and .lottie through a WASM player. The WASM and worker assets can be self-hosted with setWasmUrl()/setWorkerUrl(); the default player otherwise fetches a version-pinned WASM file from jsDelivr or unpkg. @lottiefiles/react-lottie-player and @lottiefiles/lottie-player are archived; @dotlottie/react-player is deprecated and pulls sharp. lottie-react-native is out of scope because this requirement is React DOM.
